title: Monitoring and Audit Mechanism for Imported Inputs
summary: The monitoring of imported inputs has evolved from a simple commissioner-led audit to a more structured, committee-based oversight mechanism. Over time, the process has shifted from general oversight to specific, multi-tiered committee inspections involving joint commissioners and specialized departments to ensure compliance with input-output coefficients.

evolution.institutional_oversight: Shifted from individual commissioner oversight to multi-member committee-based inspections.
evolution.procedural_rigor: Increased from simple reporting to mandatory committee-led physical verification and formal reporting structures.

timeline.change: Established the initial audit framework requiring annual estimation and 6-month interval audits by the Customs Valuation and Internal Audit Commissionerate.
Introduced the requirement for pre-import submission of input-output coefficients and 6-month physical inspections by VAT divisional officers.
Formalized the inspection process by mandating the formation of a specific committee led by a Joint Commissioner, moving away from sole reliance on divisional officers.

TABLE: The table serves as the reference document for estimating the annual requirements of production inputs based on previous year production data and current year production plans.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs at the relevant customs house or station receives the annual input requirement statements by January of each year. Based on these statements, the Commissioner authorizes the clearance of imported inputs for the applicant entity.
Commissioner, Customs Valuation and Inte: The Commissioner of this office receives the annual input requirement statements by January of each year. They are also responsible for conducting physical audits every six months to verify that imported inputs have been utilized in the actual production of goods.
Commissioner, Customs Valuation and Internal Audit Commissionerate

Commissioner of Customs Valuation and In: The Commissioner is responsible for conducting audits within the shortest possible time and submitting an objective report according to the specified format within one month of completion.
The Commissioner must submit this report to the member of the National Board of Revenue (Customs: Policy) and provide copies to the relevant Customs House or station authorities.
In cases where misused imported inputs are identified during an audit, the Commissioner shall request the concerned Customs Commissioner to initiate legal action under the Customs Act.
National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue, specifically the member responsible for customs policy, is the designated recipient of the audit report generated by the audit commissionerate.
Customs Act 1969: The Act serves as the legal basis for initiating enforcement actions against the misuse of duty-free or concessionary imported inputs as specified in the relevant penalty table.
Bonded Warehouse Operation: If an audit confirms that imported inputs were utilized correctly at the importer's establishment, the bond or undertaking provided by the importer shall be returned.

Commissioner of Customs Valuation and In: member of the National Board of Revenue (Customs: Policy)

Value Added Tax Commissionerate: The Commissioner is responsible for ensuring that imported goods, parts, or materials are being utilized for computer production in accordance with the authorized input-output coefficient.
Value Added Tax Divisional Officer: The officer acts under the authority of the Commissioner to conduct physical inspections every six months to verify the actual usage of imported components for manufacturing purposes.
Computer Manufacturing Process: The production of computers using imported inputs is subject to regular verification against authorized input-output coefficients to ensure compliance with import conditions.

Input-Output Coefficient: Manufacturers must submit three copies of the input-output coefficient documentation, including estimated wastage, to the Commissioner of the relevant VAT Commissionerate before importing raw materials or components for cellular phone production.

The approved and countersigned documentation serves as a control measure, with copies distributed to the National Board of Revenue and the manufacturing authority for record-keeping and compliance verification.
A certified photocopy of the approved input-output coefficient must be submitted alongside the bill of entry during the customs clearance process for every shipment of imported inputs.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner is responsible for reviewing and approving the input-output coefficients submitted by cellular phone manufacturers.
Upon approval, the Commissioner must countersign the documents and ensure they are distributed to the appropriate authorities for monitoring and record-keeping purposes.
National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue receives a copy of the approved input-output coefficient from the local VAT Commissionerate to maintain oversight of industrial import activities.
Bill of Entry: The bill of entry must be accompanied by a certified photocopy of the approved input-output coefficient during the customs clearance process to verify the legitimacy of imported materials.

Department of Livestock Services: The Department of Livestock Services is responsible for monitoring the utilization of imported goods by the relevant importer to ensure they are properly used in poultry or dairy farms.

This authority also works in conjunction with the Value Added Tax authorities to verify that animal feed produced from imported raw materials is effectively supplied to the designated poultry or livestock farms.
Value Added Tax: The Commissioner of Value Added Tax is mandated to monitor the end-use of imported inputs along with the Department of Livestock Services to ensure compliance in the supply chain of poultry and dairy feed production.

member_objects.resolved_text: ৩। দফা (২) এ উল্লিখিত প্রতিবেদন প্রাপ্তির পর যদি দেখা যায় যে, আমদানিকৃত উপকরণ আমদানিকারক কর্তৃক খেলনা শিল্পে আংশিকভাবে ব্যবহৃত হইয়াছে বা ব্যবহৃত হয় নাই তাহা হইলে আমদানিকারকের নিকট হইতে প্রযোজ্য হারে শুল্ক, কর এবং জরিমানা (fine) আদায়যোগ্য হইবে।

Customs Duty and Taxes: The importer is required to pay applicable customs duties and taxes if it is discovered that imported materials were only partially used in the toy industry or were not used for their intended purpose.
Penalties: In cases of non-compliance where imported goods are not fully utilized for the specified manufacturing purpose, the importer is liable to pay penalties in addition to the required customs duties and taxes.
Imported Inputs: The use of imported materials is subject to monitoring, and any failure to consume these inputs entirely within the toy industry triggers an assessment of liability for duties and penalties.

Industrial Mould: The importation of production materials must be verified against approved input-output coefficients to ensure compliance in the manufacturing of moulds or dies.
The Commissioner of the relevant VAT Commissionerate is mandated to conduct physical inspections every six months to confirm the proper utilization of imported inputs for mould or die production.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of the relevant VAT Commissionerate is responsible for ensuring oversight of production processes through periodic physical inspections of the manufacturing facilities.
Commissioner of the relevant VAT Commissionerate

member_objects.clause_title: ৭.৩ AEO প্রতিষ্ঠানের অডিট কার্যক্রমে বিশেষভাবে লক্ষ্যণীয় বিষয়সমূহ

Authorized Economic Operator: Audit activities for these entities should focus on system-based audits to ensure regulatory compliance.
When conducting post-clearance audits for these organizations, specific procedures beyond standard practices must be prioritized to verify the accuracy of declarations and internal operations.
H.S. Code: Auditors are required to verify the accuracy of these codes specifically for high-volume and high-value products to prevent misclassification.
Customs Clearance: Physical verification of goods at the premises of the authorized entity should be conducted on a random basis to ensure consistency with declared information.
Customs Computerised Entry Processing Sy: Auditors must inspect the entity's internal databases, computer systems, and software modules, particularly those related to supply chain management, to validate transaction integrity.
Customs Duty: Audit procedures must prioritize verifying the ratio of finished goods produced against total imported inputs to ensure that all relevant duties and taxes have been correctly calculated and paid.

member_objects.resolved_text: (৪) এই প্রজ্ঞাপনে উল্লেখিত যন্ত্রাংশ বা উপকরণ পরিশিষ্ট-২ অনুযায়ী আমদানি করিয়া অনুমোদিত উপকরণ-উৎপাদ সহগ মোতাবেক এয়ারকন্ডিশনার উৎপাদন হইতেছে কিনা তাহা নিশ্চিত হওয়ার জন্য সংশ্লিষ্ট ভ্যাট কমিশনারেটের কমিশনার একজন যুগ্ম কমিশনার ও সংশ্লিষ্ট ভ্যাট বিভাগের বিভাগীয় কর্মকর্তার সমন্বয়ে একটি কমিটি গঠন করিবেন। গঠিত কমিটি প্রতি ৬ (ছয়) মাস অন্তর সরেজমিন পরিদর্শন করিয়া কমিশনারের নিকট প্রতিবেদন দাখিল করিবেন। দাখিলকৃত প্রতিবেদনের সহিত আমদানিকৃত পণ্যের ব্যবহারজনিত বা অন্য কোনো অসংগতি থাকিলে তাহা খালাসকারী কাস্টম হাউস বা কাস্টমস স্টেশনকে অবহিত করিতে হইবে। ভ্যাট কমিশনারেট হইতে প্রাপ্ত প্রতিবেদনের ভিত্তিতে কাস্টম হাউস বা কাস্টমস স্টেশন যথার্থতা যাচাই সাপেক্ষে পুনঃশুল্কায়নের প্রয়োজনীয় কার্যক্রম গ্রহণ করিবে;

Verification Committee: The Commissioner of the relevant VAT Commissionerate is required to form a committee consisting of a Joint Commissioner and a Divisional Officer to verify whether imported parts or materials are being used according to the approved input-output coefficient for manufacturing air conditioners.
The committee must conduct physical inspections every six months and submit reports to the Commissioner regarding their findings.
Customs House: Upon receiving a report from the VAT Commissionerate, the Customs House or Customs Station must evaluate the findings to determine if any discrepancies exist regarding the use of imported goods.
If discrepancies are identified, the Customs House or Customs Station is responsible for initiating necessary reassessment actions for the imported products.
Value Added Tax Commissionerate: The VAT Commissionerate is responsible for supervising the inspection process and submitting reports to the Customs authorities regarding the utilization of imported inputs by manufacturers.
